summary: Sean Payton took over Denver's play-calling and went run-first, shrinking the Broncos' passing game, while Seattle is down to Emanuel Wilson in the backfield with Charbonnet unlikely to play. No college player props were posted yet for the midweek games.

NFL|00-0034348|rec.note: Payton's switch to run-first play-calling cut Denver's passing volume, Sutton has very few catches this season, and Seattle's pass defense is among the league's best against WRs.

detail.availability: Not on Denver's injury report; he is healthy.
detail.role: With Pat Bryant on IR his snaps rose to about 81% in Week 5, but he caught only 2 of 3 targets, and he had just 9 catches on 22 targets over the first four games; Troy Franklin took most of Bryant's snaps.
detail.matchup: Seattle allows the second-fewest PPR points to WRs and about 151 passing yards a game (5.5 yards per attempt), and Draft Sharks ranks it first against the pass.
detail.script: In Payton's first game calling plays Denver ran more often than it passed, with Nix at 27 attempts for 123 yards; a 40.5 total with Denver a home underdog points to a low-volume, grinding game plan.
detail.conditions: Night game at about 42F with some chance of rain; Covers ties the drop in the total partly to rain and wind in the forecast.
detail.market: Kalshi has the over at about 40.5%, so the market already leans under; the under is priced around 59.5%, above the 52.4% break-even, which shrinks the edge.
detail.experts: Draft Sharks calls Sutton a hard-to-trust WR4 while the run-heavy split lasts and names Seattle as one of the worst WR matchups on his schedule.

NFL|00-0031492|kpts.note: Seattle is a small road favorite (mostly -2.5, total 41.5-42.5) and both offenses convert poorly on third down, which tends to turn drives into field-goal tries; altitude helps long kicks.

detail.matchup: Denver gives up about 143 rushing yards a game at 4.8 per carry, so Seattle should move the ball between the 20s, while its 29.8% third-down rate (31st) points to stalled drives and field goals rather than touchdowns.
detail.script: Seattle is favored by 2.5-3 with about 21-22 implied points, and previews predict scores like 23-16 and 23-20 that usually include two or more Seattle field goals.
detail.conditions: Altitude helps distance; the light wind (about 4 mph) is fine, but a roughly 30% rain chance is a small risk.
detail.market: No Kalshi price; the total falling from 42.5 to 40.5 lowers Seattle's touchdown expectation more than its field-goal expectation.
detail.experts: Sports Betting Dime and Football Nation both project Seattle in the low 20s.

NFL|00-0036158|car.note: With Payton calling plays, Denver went run-heavy and gave Dobbins 18 carries, far above his early-season average; RJ Harvey handles the passing-down and two-minute work.

detail.role: In Week 5 Dobbins had 18 carries to Harvey's 3, after averaging about 11.5 per game in the first four weeks under Davis Webb's play-calling; Harvey took every two-minute-drill snap.
detail.matchup: Seattle is second in run defense, which hurts his yardage more than his carry count.
detail.script: A low total and a 3-point spread should keep the game close enough for Payton to stay with the run; the risk is falling behind by two scores, which shifts snaps to Harvey.
detail.conditions: Possible rain and a cool night favor a run-leaning plan.
detail.market: Kalshi has it at 50%, so the change in play-caller does not look fully priced.
detail.experts: Draft Sharks says Dobbins does best when Denver leads and can keep running, and expects Harvey to matter more in a pass-heavy game against Seattle.

NFL|00-0034869|ryd.note: Nothing concrete on Darnold's running; Denver's pass rush (five sacks of him in Week 5 came from San Francisco) could force scrambles, but that is inference only.

detail.availability: Healthy and starting; the glute injury from September is behind him, and backup Drew Lock is limited with a forearm injury.
detail.script: Darnold has five interceptions in three games since returning, and Seattle may lean on the run against Denver's weak run defense, which leaves few designed QB runs.
detail.market: Kalshi is about 49.5%, essentially a coin flip.

NFL|00-0038797|car.note: Lead back with Charbonnet unlikely to play (coach says subject to change) and Price sidelined, but he averages under 15 carries a game, so 18.5 needs a career-type workload.

detail.availability: Healthy; Macdonald said Charbonnet's answer is no for now, and Price is on IR.
detail.role: In Week 5 he had 20 carries plus 2 catches; Holani had only 4 carries.
detail.matchup: Denver allows 4.8 yards per carry and about 143 rushing yards a game.
detail.script: As the favorite in a low-total game, Seattle should stay with the run; a lost fumble in Week 5 is the only threat to his workload.

NFL|00-0039732|pyd.note: In Payton's first game calling plays Nix threw 27 times for 123 yards, and Seattle allows about 167 passing yards a game; the app's over rests on volume from before the change.

detail.role: Nix's checkdown-heavy profile (29 of 42 throws in one sample were behind the line or under 10 yards) and the new run-first plan cap his yardage.
detail.matchup: Seattle allows 5.5 yards per pass attempt, one of the league's best rates.
detail.market: Kalshi has it at about 50.5% despite the drop in the total.

NFL|00-0038543|recyd.note: Limited on both estimated reports with an ankle but expected to play; Denver's secondary may be short, with Surtain and Hufanga missing Tuesday's walkthrough and Moss limited.

detail.availability: Listed limited Monday and Tuesday on estimated (walkthrough-only) reports, and the designation is questionable; he aggravated the ankle against San Francisco but finished with 102 yards.
detail.matchup: Surtain is doubtful and Moss is questionable; Barron and Abrams-Draine started in their place in Week 5.
detail.experts: SI expects him to exploit Denver's depleted secondary if Surtain and Moss sit again.

NFL|00-0038797|td.note: Lead back with Charbonnet unlikely to play; he scored Seattle's 2-yard TD last week and has two rushing and one receiving TD this season against a Denver run defense that has struggled.

detail.availability: Healthy; Charbonnet is unlikely to be activated from PUP.
detail.role: Twenty carries in Week 5, including a 2-yard first-quarter TD; Holani is a change-of-pace and receiving back (4 carries, 4 catches).
detail.matchup: Denver allows 4.8 yards per carry and about 143 rushing yards a game.
detail.script: Seattle is favored by 3 with about 21-22 implied points, and it scored first in 14 of its last 19 games.
detail.market: Kalshi is about 43.5% and books are at +110 to +114 (about 47%), the shortest price on the board, so the market is already above the app's 38.6%.
detail.experts: Odds and red-zone previews list him first in role order and as the likeliest scorer; he is the most popular pick in this game.

NFL-SEA-at-DEN-1016.summary: Sean Payton took over Denver's play-calling in Week 5 and went run-first (Dobbins 18 carries, Nix 27 attempts for 123 yards), which limits the receivers against a Seattle defense that gives up the second-fewest WR fantasy points. Denver's secondary is banged up (Surtain and Hufanga did not practice Tuesday, Moss limited), JSN is questionable with an ankle but expected to play, the total sits around…
